phrases.latin: Tum caudam mōre atque rītū adūlantium canum clēmenter et blandē movet
phrases.english: Then, in the way of fawning dogs, it gently and coaxingly wags its tail (Androclus’s lion)
the wagtail (motacilla), because it is always wagging its tail

phrases.latin: Vidē, ut caudam movet! Gaudet tē vidēre.
phrases.english: Look how he’s wagging his tail! He’s glad to see you.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
